title: Muskan Rastogi, her lover Sahil Shukla sentenced to death in blue drum murder case
content: Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla have been sentenced to death for the murder of Muskan's husband, Saurabh Rajput. The crime, known as the blue drum murder case, involved dismembering Rajput's remains. Following a complex trial, which included 126 hearings and 22 witnesses, both were found guilty. The prosecution labeled the crime as one of the rarest of rare cases requiring the death penalty.

title: 'Why are you ruining nation?' Dipke heckled, called 'CIA agent' at Delhi airport

Later, Das and Ranka were sent to 5-day judicial custody on the order of Delhi's special executive magistrate court.

content: Satya Nadella's regret was not limited to his disagreement with the proposed acquisition. He said the experience made him think about how people in important meetings can fail to speak up even when they believe they see a problem that others may have missed

title: Diwali bonanza for railway staff: 78-day bonus cleared for 11.4 lakh employees
content: The Union Cabinet has approved a Productivity Linked Bonus for railway employees worth Rs 2,009.61 crore. It will benefit approximately 11.41 lakh eligible railway staff members across various categories. The maximum bonus that each eligible employee can receive is Rs 17,951. This annual bonus is provided ahead of the Durga Puja and Dussehra holidays to motivate employees. Railways recorded significant freight loading and passenger numbers during the 2025-26 period.

title: Maine chef rebuilt career after losing restaurant; now gets 60,000 booking cards a year
content: Erin French's remarkable journey saw her battling through addiction, enduring depression, and facing a heartbreaking divorce that led to the closure of her restaurant. Returning to her roots in Freedom, she innovatively launched pop-up dining events, rekindling her culinary passion. In 2014, she triumphantly reopened The Lost Kitchen in a refurbished mill, emphasizing seasonal, locally sourced goods, with a unique postcard reservation system that draws about 60,000 requests each year.

title: Former Morgan Stanley CEO’s $13.5m Manhattan home now lists for $80m
content: John Mack and his wife Christy are putting their lavish Upper East Side townhouse on the market for a staggering $80 million. Selling at this price would establish a new benchmark for townhouses in New York City. Since purchasing it in 2009, they have extensively renovated the property, resulting in a 16,000-square-foot masterpiece that boasts upscale features such as a wellness club and exclusive guest quarters.

title: US ends 540-day grace period for immigrants after work authorisation expires
content: In a significant policy shift, the US Department of Homeland Security has abolished the 540-day automatic extension for work permits. This development results in immediate loss of work authorization for many, particularly affecting H-4 visa holders and asylum seekers, even while their renewal applications are pending. Moreover, the USCIS continues to face notable delays in processing these renewals, leading to a legal challenge from impacted parties contesting the new regulation.

title: Why some people rehearse what to say before phone calls, according to psychology
content: When gearing up for a phone call, it’s crucial to practice your introduction and main talking points to boost how effectively you communicate. Many face phone anxiety caused by unexpected inquiries or interpretations from the other end. Studies indicate this anxiety stems from one’s comfort with various communication styles and language proficiency. While rehearsals are beneficial, overthinking can amplify worries about what to say.

title: Now, RCF-made Vande Bharat Express completes 180 kmph speed trial successfully
content: RCF Kapurthala has successfully tested a new 16-coach Vande Bharat Express train set at high speeds. The testing occurred at 180 kilometers per hour on the Mathura–Nagda section of railway. This development is part of Indian Railways' expansion of advanced trains since 2019. The upgraded train includes improved safety features and greater passenger conveniences, enhancing the travel experience.

title: Anti-drug activist murder: Bulldozers raze accused’s house, shop set ablaze in Punjab
content: In a significant move, authorities have demolished the residence of Ashwani Kumar, the prime suspect in the murder of activist Parwinder Singh Jhota. Following Kumar's arrest in Rajasthan, protests erupted in Mansa as citizens rallied for justice. In response to public outrage, a Punjab bandh has been declared, reflecting the community's demand for accountability in the wake of this tragedy.

title: India rebuilding ties with China? Here’s what Piyush Goyal said
content: India is working to strengthen its relations with China, emphasizing the need for fair trade agreements and consistent engagement. The trade deficit with China has widened, raising concerns for India's economic outlook. Efforts are underway to enhance semiconductor cooperation with Singapore, focusing on workforce training. India is also fostering strong ties with the United States across various sectors, promoting trade and defense collaborations.

title: Rihanna gave $1.75m for Barbados cancer care; centre still treats patients
content: In 2012, Rihanna made a generous donation of $1.75 million in medical equipment to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Barbados, honoring her late grandmother Clara Brathwaite. This contribution not only modernized the hospital's cancer-care services but also established the Clara Brathwaite Centre. Today, it plays a crucial role in delivering essential cancer treatments like chemotherapy and radiotherapy, significantly enhancing healthcare accessibility for the community.

title: Cardboard garden beds cut weed cover to 15% by second season in USDA trial
content: Weeds can significantly impact crop yield, leading to a need for effective control methods. A USDA-funded trial demonstrated that cardboard beds reduced weed coverage compared to tilled beds. Farmers found that using cardboard made weeding easier and more efficient after two growing seasons. The results from the trial showed varied crop yields when grown in different bed types.

title: 'Manager's wife attacked with bottles': Beer spill, brawl and a killing at Delhi club
content: Daljeet Singh, a 29-year-old driver, died after being assaulted at a club in Inderlok. An argument over spilled beer escalated into a violent altercation involving club staff and security personnel. Daljeet was reportedly beaten for nearly an hour before being locked in a room. His condition worsened after returning home, leading to his hospitalization and subsequent death.

title: From 'Indira Gandhi' to 'PM': Cabinet takes up proposal to rename 4 pension schemes
content: The Union Cabinet is set to revamp a range of social welfare programs previously named after Indira Gandhi. By prefixing these initiatives linked to pensions for the elderly, widows, and disabled individuals with 'PM', the administration seeks to modernize their appeal. Notably, the National Social Assistance Programme will be renamed PM Shayata Yojna to reinforce this updated branding strategy.

title: Rajnath Singh pitches joint defence production with ASEAN countries
content: Defence minister Rajnath Singh highlighted the pressing necessity for enhanced defence collaboration between India and ASEAN nations. He advocated for the joint production of military technologies and improvements in counter-drone capabilities, cyber defence, and maritime monitoring. Singh emphasized the significance of cost-effective defence innovations in contemporary warfare, referencing recent drone conflicts.

title: 'We immediately think of Chris Gayle': Pujara's big statement on Abhishek Sharma
content: The third T20I against the West Indies was another milestone match for Abhishek Sharma. He became the sixth Indian men's cricketer to score 2,000 runs in T20 internationals. He also became the fastest batter in men's cricket to reach the milestone in terms of balls faced.

title: How constant stress at home can affect children’s behaviour and confidence
content: Daily responsibilities can often leave parents feeling inundated, affecting how they relate to their children. This stress may translate into noticeable emotional or behavioral shifts in kids, indicative of their internal struggles. Establishing a welcoming atmosphere for children to communicate their feelings is vital. By acknowledging their own stress and responding appropriately, parents can better support their children. Prioritizing their own well-being is essential for nurturing healthy family connections.

title: Air India Frankfurt-Delhi flight diverted to Jaipur; pilot pressed hijack code
content: Air India flight inbound from Frankfurt to Delhi was redirected to Jaipur due to a suspected hijack threat. The pilot took immediate action by activating the hijack alert code while flying over the Mumbai Flight Information Region. After a safe landing in Jaipur, the aircraft was moved to an isolated area for comprehensive security evaluations.

title: EU proposes one-year delay to methane rules for oil and gas imports
content: The European Commission has recommended postponing the enforcement of methane emissions regulations concerning oil and gas imports. This shift comes amid pressure from nations like France and the United States, focusing on energy supply challenges. Concerns regarding potential expenses and compliance issues raised by EU member states have also played a role.

title: Woman applies for 130 shares, bank enters 65; commission awards Rs 37,000, not Rs 40L
content: In 2022, the woman applied for 130 shares in an IPO. However, the bank recorded her application for just 65 shares, which she claimed resulted in a loss of Rs 42,142. She also accused the bank of causing her physical and mental harassment. The Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission subsequently partly allowed the woman’s appeal.

title: Oscar Whitfield wins Young Wildlife Photographer title with dung beetle image

Notable winners included Federico Veronesi, Amelie Davis, and James Lewin, each celebrated for their stunning depictions of wildlife. The captivating exhibition showcasing these masterpieces will commence at the Natural History Museum on Friday, 16 October 2026.

title: Arizona brothers, 10 and 12, found safe after 8-hour desert search

A collaborative effort involving local businesses and rescue teams, along with aerial support from the Arizona Department of Public Safety, led to their discovery six miles from home, with one boy still barefoot.

title: Air India cancelled flight, passengers left stranded; commission orders Rs 1.34L payout

This followed the cancellation of a connecting flight from New Delhi to Toronto without proper notification. The complainant had previously booked the journey and incurred additional costs due to the cancellation. The commission found that the companies exhibited deficiency in service and unfair trade practices.

title: Delhi fire scare: People jump from first floor as flames break out at Maujpur restaurant
content: In a dramatic scene late Tuesday night, flames engulfed the kitchen of Udham Fish Point restaurant in Maujpur. Witnesses describe the moment when a woman jumped to a nearby terrace in a bid to evade the fire. Quick-thinking staff were able to extinguish the blaze before it escalated, and fortunately, there were no injuries. Authorities are now investigating the incident to uncover what sparked the fire.

title: BFI suspends secretary general Pramod Kumar over alleged financial irregularities

BFI president Ajay Singh issued the suspension order on Tuesday, pending an inquiry into the allegations against Kumar. These include issuing a work order for broadcasting arrangements without the required approval.

title: The battle against inflation is entering a tougher phase: What it means for you
content:
India’s retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September, its highest level in nearly two years, driven by rising food, fuel and transport costs.

Rural households have been hit particularly hard, with food inflation crossing 8%. The surge comes amid elevated global crude oil prices, a weakening rupee and continuing uncertainty in West Asia. With inflation nearing the RBI’s upper tolerance limit, questions are growing over whether another interest rate hike could be on the horizon.

This explainer examines what’s driving inflation, why food prices are rising and what it could mean for consumers, investors and the broader economy.

title: Preventive detention explained: Know your constitutional rights
content:
The detentions during the October 10 protests have brought renewed attention to preventive detention, constitutional protections and the limits of state power.

What is preventive detention? When can authorities legally detain someone without trial? What protections does Article 22 of the Constitution provide? And what did the Supreme Court say about detentions, mobility restrictions and the right to peaceful protest?

This explainer breaks down the legal framework governing preventive detention, Section 163 of the BNSS, and the constitutional safeguards available to citizens in India.

title: 3 killed in Russian missile & drone barrage, 600,000 left without power in Ukraine
content: the attack left at least 600,000 people without electricity, authorities say . a large-scale overnight missile and drone attack in Kyiv killed at least three people . the attacks have damaged equipment at 26 elements of power system facilities and four oil systems .

title: Why Munir's plan to 'split' up Pakistan may spell the end of civilian govt
content: field marshal Asim Munir is considering a radical solution to governance problems . he is considering breaking up the country's four provinces into 12 to 15 smaller provinces . smaller units, according to the argument for restructuring, would be easier to govern . but in a country where the military has long wielded influence over civilian governments, the political question is whether they would also be easy to control .

title: William Shatner’s kidney stone sold for $75,000, helping a Louisiana family get a home
